title: Find the original amount before a percent change (a salary is $93 940 after a 122% increase — what was it?)

lesson.title: Working Backwards From a Big Percent Jump

steps.say: You already know how to go forwards: if something grows by three point two five percent, you multiply by one point zero three two five. Today we flip that around. Someone tells you the salary AFTER a one hundred twenty-two percent raise, and you have to figure out what it was BEFORE.

Here is the whole idea in one picture. The original salary is one full bar, one hundred percent. A one hundred twenty-two percent increase adds another chunk that is even bigger than the original, one hundred twenty-two percent. Stack them and the new salary is two hundred twenty-two percent of the original. So new equals two point two two times original.

visual.caption: The raise is bigger than the original amount

steps.say: Now put the real number in. Two point two two times the original equals ninety-three thousand nine hundred forty dollars. To find the original I undo the multiplying, so I divide. Ninety-three thousand nine hundred forty divided by two point two two is about forty-two thousand three hundred fifteen dollars and thirty-two cents. That is the salary before the raise.

Watch the trap. Lots of people divide by one point two two instead, and they get exactly seventy-seven thousand dollars, which looks beautifully clean. But test it: seventy-seven thousand with a one hundred twenty-two percent raise becomes seventy-seven thousand times two point two two, which is one hundred seventy thousand nine hundred forty dollars. Way too big. A clean-looking answer is not a correct answer. And never try subtracting one point two two from one, because that gives you a negative salary, and nobody gets paid minus twenty thousand dollars.

visual.caption: Dividing by 1.22 overshoots by a lot

steps.say: So the rule to carry with you: to undo a percent increase, divide by one plus the percent as a decimal. For a one hundred twenty-two percent raise that is two point two two, not one point two two. Then always grow your answer forwards to check it lands back where you started.

lesson.answer: To undo a percent increase, divide the new amount by 1 plus the percent — a 122% raise means dividing by 2.22.

practice.question: A rare hockey card sold on a Vancouver trading site for $310 after its value went up 150%. Draw yourself a bar model: one bar for the original value at 100 percent, and a second bar on top of it for the 150 percent increase. What total percent do the two bars make together, and what was the card worth before the increase?
practice.answer: The two bars make 250 percent, so the selling price is 2.5 times the original value. That gives 310 divided by 2.5, which is $124. Check it: 124 times 2.5 equals 310. Correct. (Dividing by 1.5 would give about $206.67, and 206.67 grown by 150 percent is about $516.67 — far too big.)
